_note: Board profiles, versioned DATA (docs/backlog/pcb-board-profile-prototype.md). One row per profile; precis.pcb.profiles.profile_rules(name) is the only reader. A rule omitted from a row is OFF (None). Every set rule is {value, why}: the value is a floor/ceiling applied ON TOP of the fab capability row (it can raise a number, never take one below jlc_min), the why is the one-line reason it exists. 'prod' is the all-off row: today's behaviour exactly. Tune a prototype figure here, not in code.

rows.name: prod
rows.label: production board, machine assembled once (the default)

rows.name: prototype
rows.label: prototype board, hand assembled, probed and reworked

trace_width_mm.why: survives a lifted pad and iron heat; legible on a scope

trace_spacing_mm.why: solder bridges and probe tips stay off the neighbour

drill_mm.why: a wire-wrap or probe wire fits; the drill survives rework

annular_ring_mm.why: unchanged from the house tier; via diameter follows drill + 2 x ring, the ring is not the lever

via_body_cost_mm.why: soft router cost for a via under a part's courtyard, in wire-length mm; a detour of up to this much extra wire beats the via; a cost, never a keep-out

via_density_max_per_mm2.why: at most 1 via per 4 mm2 in any window; vias are what a person has to dig past

via_density_window_mm.why: the limit is on windows, not the board average

via_density_step_mm.why: window slide step over the outline bounding box

thermal_spokes.why: hand soldering a pad tied to a plane pulls the heat away

thermal_spoke_width_mm.why: at least the prototype trace-width floor

thermal_gap_mm.why: antipad gap between pad and pour

refdes_height_mm.why: a person reads the board; the label has to survive a magnifier-free glance

strict_fields.why: the profile's numbers are the new floor; a warn on a number the profile set is noise

checks.why: prototype-only findings; prod never emits these rule names
